themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Surge
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints spiked to 7 this week versus a baseline of 1.0 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 600% increase (z-score: 8.49)—suggesting either a disease outbreak, pest infestation, or environmental hazard emerging in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights this week.
evidence: 7 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (600% spike)
Z-score of 8.49 indicates statistically severe anomaly
Spike is concentrated in current week, not distributed over time
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Sanitation and Department of Health to identify what caused the spike—disease outbreak, rat die-off, or other environmental event
Interview residents in neighborhoods with highest concentration of complaints to document public health concerns and street conditions

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints jumped to 7 this week compared to 0.6 average weekly over 8 weeks—a 1020% spike (z-score: 6.43)—potentially signaling enforcement crackdowns, resident backlash to expanded sidewalk dining, or new violations emerging this week.
evidence: 7 outdoor dining complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1020% spike)
Z-score of 6.43 indicates statistically extreme anomaly
Timing aligns with spring season (Gothamist article 4/13 notes 'spring may finally be here')
reporting_angles: Determine if NYC Buildings or Department of Consumer Affairs launched a targeted enforcement sweep on outdoor dining permits this week
Identify which restaurants or blocks are generating complaints and why—sidewalk obstruction, noise, seating overflow, or permit violations

themes_detail.label: Real-Time Enforcement Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Real-time enforcement complaints surged to 8 this week versus 0.9 weekly average—an 814% increase (z-score: 4.41)—suggesting a sudden shift in police or agency enforcement activity or new tactics deployed in the district this week.
evidence: 8 real-time enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (814% spike)
Z-score of 4.41 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Correlates with 1100% spike in 'Investigations and Discipline' complaints (3 this week vs 0.2 avg)
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD and city enforcement agencies to determine if new policing strategy or enforcement initiative was rolled out this week
Interview residents and community leaders about nature of complaints—traffic stops, street checks, quality-of-life enforcement, or other activity

themes_detail.label: Investigations & Discipline Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Complaints related to Investigations and Discipline (likely NYPD-related) jumped to 3 this week versus 0.2 average—a 1100% spike (z-score: 6.35)—potentially indicating resident friction with police conduct or misconduct allegations emerging this week.
evidence: 3 IAD complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1100% spike)
Z-score of 6.35 indicates statistically extreme anomaly
Converges with 814% spike in real-time enforcement complaints (8 this week vs 0.9 avg)
reporting_angles: Request CCRB (Civilian Complaint Review Board) data to determine what misconduct allegations or complaint types are driving the spike
Investigate whether specific incidents or police actions in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights this week triggered complaints or social media discussion

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes & Park Rule Violations
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints hit 3 this week versus 0.2 baseline (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35), and park rule violations surged 3 complaints 2 weeks ago versus 0.2 average—signaling emerging quality-of-life issues or enforcement inconsistencies in public spaces.
evidence: 3 abandoned bike complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
3 park rule violation complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
Overlaps with Streetsblog NYC article (4/13) on 'Rampant Placard Abuse' mucking up bike lanes in downtown Brooklyn
reporting_angles: Map locations of abandoned bikes to identify hotspots and determine if bike-share or personal bikes are accumulating due to lack of DSNY/Parks enforcement
Investigate whether Parks Department enforcement capacity has changed or whether residents are using 311 as a workaround for slow removal times
